name: Alameda
address: Rua da Polícia de Segurança Pública 10, 8000 Faro
tier: THE BERTHS · THE STARRED TABLES — FARO'S FIRST STAR AND THE TWO-STAR KITCHENS OF THE COAST
recognition: MICHELIN Guide Portugal 2026: one star, awarded 10 March 2026, the first ever in Faro
what_to_order: Origami tasting menu|'O amor além do tempo' legends menu|Alameda menu|Ria Formosa oyster|Octopus|Vegetarian tasting menu
price_range: MICHELIN €€€ (seen Oct 2026); Guía Repsol lists a 9-course tasting at €115 (undated)
notes: The chef's Origami tasting menu, with the wine pairing
verdict: The star announced in Funchal on 10 March 2026 is the first Faro has ever held, and it puts a serious dinner fifteen minutes on foot from the marina, with no drive to the resort coast. The price sits in MICHELIN's €€€ band, below the two-star houses. Hours differ across listings, so book by phone and confirm the day before promising it to guests.
caveat: Tasting menus only, no à la carte; closed Tuesday and Wednesday per MICHELIN, but listings differ: call ahead

name: Vila Joya
address: Estrada da Galé, Praia da Galé, 8201-902 Albufeira
tier: THE STARRED TABLES — FARO'S FIRST STAR AND THE TWO-STAR KITCHENS OF THE COAST
recognition: MICHELIN Guide Portugal 2026: two stars renewed, held since 1999 (first star 1995)
notes: The evening tasting menu on the terrace
verdict: The longest-held two stars on the coast, renewed in the March 2026 guide, and the one to book when the night has to be the grand one. It is a forty-minute drive from Faro and priced accordingly. The house has historically closed from November to February, so it fits a late-October dinner, not a December one, unless the hotel says otherwise.
caveat: Winter closure (historically Nov-Feb) not dated for 2026-27: call before planning; phone numbers differ across listings

name: Ocean
tier: THE STARRED TABLES — FARO'S FIRST STAR AND THE TWO-STAR KITCHENS OF THE COAST
recognition: MICHELIN Guide Portugal 2026: two stars renewed; Best Service Award 2025 to Nelson Marreiros
what_to_order: Sabores da Descoberta tasting menu|Codfish with Alentejo citrus|Skate from the Berlengas|Azores pineapple dessert
verdict: The most polished service on the coast: its restaurant manager, Nelson Marreiros, took MICHELIN's Best Service Award in 2025, and the two stars were renewed in March 2026. It is a fifty-minute drive and a full evening. Ocean takes a winter break and reopened only on 5 March in 2025, so check before promising it to guests after October.
caveat: Dinner only, closed Mon-Tue per Portugal Resident; winter break dates for 2026-27 not found

name: Estaminé (Ilha Deserta)
address: Ilha da Barreta (Ilha Deserta), Faro; Animaris boats from the old-town waterfront (listings name the Porta Nova pier or the Cais das Portas do Mar)
tier: TABLES WITH A STORY — A LUNCH ON AN ISLAND WITH NO ROAD, AND A CHEF'S SMALL ROOM INSIDE THE WALLS
recognition: The only restaurant on Ilha da Barreta, reached only by boat; rebuilt 2021 after a fire, solar-powered
what_to_order: Arroz de lingueirão|Grilled sea bream|Ria Formosa oysters|Conquilhas|Tuna and octopus estupetas
reservation: Book with Animaris, boat and table together
notes: Arroz de lingueirão, the wet razor-clam rice
verdict: The lunch that turns a day in Faro into a day on the water, and the reason to book the boat. The cooking is simple, grilled fish and rice, and the setting carries it. Out of high season it runs on reservation, and the ferry timetable decides how long you stay: call Animaris before you plan anything after October.
caveat: Boat access only; after September it may open by reservation only: book boat and table together

name: CHECKin by Leonel Pereira
tier: TABLES WITH A STORY — A LUNCH ON AN ISLAND WITH NO ROAD, AND A CHEF'S SMALL ROOM INSIDE THE WALLS
recognition: Listed in the MICHELIN Guide (€€); Bib Gourmand since 2021, not re-confirmed for 2026
what_to_order: Cozinhados no Tacho|Check-in starters|Momentos Especiais|Check-out desserts|Portuguese wine by the sommelier
reservation: Recommended; by phone (not bookable on the MICHELIN site)
notes: A pot dish from the 'Cozinhados no Tacho' section
verdict: The best-priced serious dinner in the Cidade Velha, and the one to send a guest who wants a chef's cooking without a tasting-menu evening. MICHELIN lists it at €€. The Bib was confirmed in 2021 and Fodor's says it has held one since opening, but we found no 2026 list naming it, so call it MICHELIN-listed until the Bib is rechecked.
caveat: Dinner only, closed Sunday per MICHELIN; not bookable via MICHELIN, phone ahead

name: Tasca do Ricky
tier: THE BERTHS · THE TASCAS — WHERE FARO EATS
recognition: Nine tables, no more than four guests each; no bookings June-September (house listing on Tableagent)
what_to_order: Cataplana de marisco|Arroz de lingueirão|Grilled fish of the day|Amêijoas à bulhão pato
reservation: No reservations June-September per the house's own listing (first come); outside those months book ahead; tables limited to four guests
notes: Cataplana de marisco, the one the owner recommends that night
verdict: The tasca to put first on a Faro list when the guest wants the regional repertoire cooked straight. Ratings vary by platform and a minority of diners mention uneven service, but the cataplana is the constant in every account. It is dinner only on most listings, and the room is too small for a crew table: divide it into fours or go elsewhere.
caveat: Tables of four maximum; no bookings June-September (first come), so book in the off-season; hours conflict, call ahead
hot_this_month: The cataplana for the first cool evenings; summer's no-booking rule is over, so call ahead — dinner Monday to Saturday by its listings.

name: A Venda
recognition: Petiscos made from scratch with a large vegetarian and vegan list (Wanderlog, Restaurantji reviews)
what_to_order: Pork stew|Fish soup|Tempura green beans|Prawns|Pork cheeks|Chocolate fondant with banana
notes: A spread of the day's petiscos, with the pork stew among them
verdict: The right table when guests want to share a dozen small plates rather than commit to one pot. It is inexpensive, the cooking is homemade, and it handles mixed tables of meat-eaters and vegetarians without fuss. The room is small, some find service slow, and it may close for the winter: do not promise it for November without a call.
caveat: Small room, book; cash only per a reviewer; one listing says it closes for the winter until February

name: Adega Nova
recognition: Known for picanha na pedra, cooked by the diner on a hot stone (Fodor's)
what_to_order: Picanha na pedra|Grilled sardines|Pork stew|Grilled fish and seafood skewers|Choco frito
reservation: Walk-in; call for a large table
notes: Picanha na pedra, cooked on the hot stone at the table
verdict: The value address of central Faro, and the place to feed a large crew without a plan. Expect noise, long shared-style tables and occasional confusion with orders. Bring cash: reviewers say it is cash only and signed as such, though one official listing says cards are accepted. Opening days conflict across listings, so ring before a weekend.
caveat: Cash only per reviewers (VisitPortugal says cards); opening days conflict across listings, call ahead
hot_this_month: Grilled fish, or the picanha on its hot stone, in the big walk-in room for the first cool evenings; its listed days disagree, so call.

name: Mercado Municipal de Faro
address: Largo Dr. Francisco Sá Carneiro, 8000-151 Faro
tier: LA RUE — THE TWO MARKETS AND THE BIFANA
recognition: Faro's covered municipal market; current building's 19th anniversary marked 21 Feb 2026 (Postal do Algarve)
what_to_order: Bifana|Fish and shellfish of the day|Fruit and vegetables
notes: A bifana at Snack Bar da Xica before the fish stalls
verdict: A working market, not a show: smaller and plainer than Olhão's, useful for provisioning in the centre and for a fast breakfast. Go early, when the fish is laid out and the bifana counter is busy. Stall hours vary and no official schedule surfaced, so check the day before you plan a galley run around it.
caveat: Mornings are best; official hours not found, stalls keep their own
hot_this_month: A morning market: the day's fish and shellfish, then a bifana at the counter before the boats go out.

name: Mercado de Olhão
tier: THE BERTHS · LA RUE — THE TWO MARKETS AND THE BIFANA
recognition: Elected one of the Novas 7 Maravilhas de Portugal, final in Sintra, 12 Sep 2026 (Postal do Algarve)
what_to_order: Sardines|Amêijoa-boa|Octopus|Ria Formosa salt and flor de sal
notes: The Saturday-morning fish hall, then the outdoor stalls
verdict: The best fish market on this coast and the one to show a chef: lagoon clams, octopus, the morning's sardines, Ria Formosa salt outside. It is a morning place; by eleven it is winding down. The 2026 award will bring more visitors, so arrive early, and on Saturday come before nine for the boats and the outdoor stalls.
caveat: Mornings only; hours unofficial; busiest Saturday
hot_this_month: Mornings from about 07:00: go before 09:00 for the boats' fish and the lagoon's clams and oysters; on Saturday the outdoor market is on the front.

name: Snack Bar da Xica
address: Mercado Municipal de Faro, Largo Dr. Francisco Sá Carneiro 10-11, 8000-151 Faro
tier: LA RUE — THE TWO MARKETS AND THE BIFANA
recognition: Bifana counter inside Faro's municipal market, cash only (Tripadvisor)
notes: Two bifanas and a small beer at the counter
verdict: The city's breakfast bifana, and the cheapest good thing in this guide. It is a counter, not a restaurant: stand, eat two, pay cash, move on. Nothing dated 2026 surfaced, so treat it as likely but not proven to be trading, and keep the market itself as the fallback if the shutter is down.
caveat: Cash only; mornings only, closed Monday per Tripadvisor; no 2026-dated confirmation found
hot_this_month: The bifana and a small beer on a market morning: the warm bite for a cool late-October start.
